body:
pranav: Heads-up — running some perf sweeps on MI250 pools and hit a kernel lookup mismatch causing conditional routing to fall through to CPU path on 4% of requests :eyes:

julia: Any repro steps or logs? which model / seqlen distribution?

pranav: repro on `gptj-6b` quantized-int8, seqlen ~ 102-320. Repro rate higher for seqlen > 192. Attached snippet from runtime lookup:
```
KERNEL_LOOKUP hit: false
requested_opset: aten::matmul
available_kernels: [mi250_fused_attn_v1(seq<=128), mi250_matmul_fp16, mi250_matmul_int8(seq<=192)]
runtime_decision: fallback_to_cpu
```

alex: That log suggests the int8 kernel has a seqlen cap at 192 so anything >192 falls out. Why did we get `hit: false` though — should have selected `mi250_matmul_fp16` instead of CPU.

dani: Could be the autotuner prefers int8 but then fails to pick fp16 if int8 policy matches but kernel selector returns no compatible kernel. Maybe a signature mismatch (opset vs kernel metadata).

rocm-bot: probe results for mi250 kernel registry at 2101023459
```
mi250_matmul_int8: present
mi250_matmul_fp16: present
mi250_fused_attn_v1: present
mi250_matmul_int8.meta: max_seqlen=192, op_signature=matmul_v2
runtime_indexer: matched_op_signature=matmul_v1
```

julia: Ah — `matmul_v2` vs `matmul_v1` mismatch. Tying back to the model compilation step we rolled yesterday. Autotune wrote kernels with new signature but runtime expects old.

pranav: That would explain the `hit: false` because runtime op signature filter rejects kernels even when they exist. How widespread is this? any traffic %?

observability-bot: Trace aggregate (last 1h): total_calls=18.2k, cpu_fallback_calls=735 (4.03%), avg_latency_cpu_fallback=420ms, avg_latency_gpu=55ms

alex: Oof. 4% is non-trivial. CPU fallbacks are expensive. We need immediate mitigation and a proper fix. Proposal:
- short-term: broaden signature matcher to allow `matmul_v1` <-> `matmul_v2` when semantics unchanged (soft-match flag)
- short-term 2: route overflow seqlen >192 to `mi250_matmul_fp16` explicitly (skip int8 selector)
- long-term: regenerate kernel metadata during autotune to include legacy signatures and seqlen variants

dani: Can we add a conditional route policy that matches model id + profile and forces `fp16` fallback for seqlen>192? That avoids changing signature matcher.

julia: Yes, we have per-model routing rules. Quick patch idea (runtime config):
```
route_rules:
  - match: {model: gptj-6b, seqlen_gt: 192}
    prefer_kernels: [mi250_matmul_fp16]
    soft_fallback: true
```

pranav: I'll push that rule to staging and roll to prod as a canary for the affected pools. Need someone to own test and watch KV cache behavior — shouldn't interfere with prefix caching.

dani: I'll smoke-test with KV cache enabled. Concern: changing kernel (int8->fp16) may change KV memory layout or serialization subtlety? Usually KV is agnostic to matmul path, but need to verify kv hits and cacheability.

alex: Also regenerate autotune profiles for mi250 pool, include both seqlen=128/192/320 samples. I'll start a job to rerun autotune and publish kernels with `op_signature` aliases.

pranav: Quick experiment results from staging after rule applied (5k requests):
- cpu_fallback: 0
- route_to_fp16: 12.6% (for seqlen>192)
- p50 latency: 68ms (vs 420ms when CPU fallback)
- p95 latency: 210ms

julia: Nice. Any cost delta due to higher GPU ops? should still be cheaper than CPU fallback.

observability-bot: Cost estimate delta (staging 1h): +3.8% GPU token cost, -72% CPU fallback cost. Net +1.4% overall.

dani: KV cache check: all cache keys match, no serialization errors, kv hit-rate unchanged.

alex: Action items:
- [alex] regenerate autotune profiles + publish kernel alias metadata (include `matmul_v1` alias) — ETA 24h
- [pranav] roll per-model route rule to prod as canary in affected pool — ETA 2h
- [dani] run KV cache regressions and full e2e smoke (includes large seqlen blast) — ETA 6h
- [julia] add a runtime CI test that asserts kernel op_signature compatibility during deploy — ETA 48h

pranav: I'll leave the canary running and watch traces. Ping me if you see any regressions. Thanks :thumbsup:

julia: Good catch. We should add a pre-deploy hook to autotune that cross-checks runtime matcher semantics.

alex: I'll also create a short incident note if the canary shows any issue. For now, prefer soft routing over global signature relax.

pranav: logging plan: add an alert when cpu_fallback_rate > 1% for any mi250 pool for 5m window. Lower threshold is noisy but worth it.

observability-bot: Alert rule created by pranav at 2101023688

dani: will update the runbook with the new interim routing rule and rollback steps.

pranav: thanks everyone — closing thread unless someone has objections.

julia: nope all good, closing :white_check_mark:
